newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines on track to meet growth targets - govt.
newsitem.headline: Philippines on track to meet growth targets - govt.

text.p: The government's economic planning body, the National Economic Development Authority (NEDA), said on Wednesday the Philippines is on track to meet its growth targets this year despite the weakness in the peso.
"The recent peso depreciation appears not to have disturbed the economy's growth prospects for the year," the NEDA said in a statement.

"Despite the jitters caused by the peso fall and lately by the oil price increase, the economy's sound fundamentals are likely to prevent a major recalculation of gross national product and inflation targets," it said.
Economic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito said the low inflation of 4.8 percent in July indicated the country was still in a position to maintain its annual inflation target of six to 6.5 percent.
Exports also showed robust growth of about 22 percent for the first half of the year, he said.
The government expects a seven to eight percent GNP growth this year.
"The expected increase in net exports and the earnings abroad will offset the dampening effects of the peso depreciation on the industry sector such as construction and manufacturing," NEDA said.
It also said the government had opted to retain a budget surplus target of 13 billion pesos in 1997 and 16 billion pesos in 1998.
